newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB yields may test lows as fears of rate rise ebb.
newsitem.headline: JGB yields may test lows as fears of rate rise ebb.

text.p: The benchmark 182nd Japanese government bond (JGB) may soon test its early-April record low yield of 2.075 percent, as fears of interest rate rises later this year fade, bond traders said on Friday.

The yield on the key 10-year cash bond had fallen briefly to 2.165 percent by Friday afternoon, the lowest since April 24, on a bearish Bank of Japan (BOJ) economic outlook released on Thursday and statements from an opposition politician that Japan should not raise interest rates this year.

"It seems fairly clear that we are now in a phase in which the market will take a shot at the record low and perhaps break below 2.0 percent, maybe even within the next month," said Naohiro Honda, deputy general manager of the bond trading department at Sanwa Bank.

The BOJ said that, while Japan's economy was continuing on a moderate recovery trend, this recovery was unlikely to gather significant momentum in view of fragility in some sectors and continued pressure from balance-sheet adjustments.

It added that capital spending was also unlikely to gather significant momentum for the time being due to an absence of rapidly expanding industries and remaining balance-sheet adjustment pressures, and that market expectations of higher interest rates were not as strong as before.

Traders said the report confirmed growing market suspicions that a near-term rise in Japanese interest rates is highly unlikely. "In fact, you could say this was almost the same as saying rates won't be raised for a while," added Sanwa's Honda.

The report emphasised comments by Yoshio Suzuki, a key opposition party member of the Lower House and a former BOJ executive director, who said on Wednesday that Japan should not raise interest rates this year as it could harm the economy and financial institutions.

Traders said that, while nobody in the market had expected a rate rise before October at the earliest, the combination of these statements and the BOJ report pushed expectations back even further and sent JGB futures briefly to 126.02 on Friday, a three-month high. JGB prices move inversely to yields.

A likely absence of selling factors and thin conditions in August, when many operators take vacations, are likely to exaggerate moves and make it easier for yields to plumb new depths, one trust bank trader said. "I'd say we could test 2.075 percent as early as next week and maybe even move below two percent within a month," he added.

Others were doubtful, however. "While it's certain that the chance of any near-term interest rate rise is fading, it's still too early to say decisively that yields will fall that much. Expect a gradual downward drift," said Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities Co Ltd's research group.
Traders said one key factor for the market could be June industrial production numbers, due out on July 30, with poor figures possibly sending yields rapidly lower.

Fuji's Ueno said that yields are likely to drift only as low as 2.15 percent or possibly 2.10 percent in the next week, while buying may be inhibited by memories of the JGBs' quick drop after their previous April rise.

JGB yields rose sharply and prices entered a downtrend on April 25 after operations were suspended at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, the first such suspension among domestic insurers in the postwar period. The move triggered fears of higher interest rates, as Japan's low interest rate policy had been blamed for low returns on investments by Nissan Life and other institutions.
